content.intro: In this lesson, you will study understanding bytecode with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you understand what the compiler and runtime each do when a program is built and launched. In this lesson, focus on why java generates bytecode and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Java source is compiled to class-file bytecode that a compatible JVM can execute. Native libraries, file paths, runtime versions, and platform assumptions can still affect portability. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect why java generates bytecode with the relationship between bytecode and the jvm before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.
